params.body:
This watch has published `broken` every day since 14 September, six verdicts in a row, on a
single line:

```
BROKEN gateway: the measured binary is not the release asset (315c4e8ca125bdd4…)
```

Nothing is wrong with the evidence. The checker was too old to read it.

`CONTROL_TAG` stood at v0.16.4 while the gateway moved through v0.17 to v0.29.0. The same
store, the same identity log, the same anchors, checked with `cmd/verify` built from
v0.29.0, gives:

```
holds  gateway: the records name release v0.29.0, whose asset matches its published sha256
holds  gateway: the measured binary is the release asset
exit code 0 · 35 holds · 0 broken
```

So the pin moves to v0.29.0.

The comment above the check said the checker's tag "need not match the machine". That was
the sentence that let this run for six days, so it is replaced by what actually holds: the
checker need not be the reference, but it does have to be able to read what the machine
writes, and the tag has to move with the gateway's releases.

**What this does not fix.** Nobody was told. This repository is where an outsider looks to
see whether the Proof-of-Control claim stands, and it said `broken` to the world for six
days with no alarm anywhere. It surfaced by accident, in a mail filter. A watch that fails
silently is the thing this whole design exists to prevent, and that part is still open.
params.title: De checker op v0.29.0
